claims.statement: For an original leaf v of any finite tree T and any integer k, with H=T-{v,s_v} and R=T-N_T[s_v], P_{T-v}=P_H+zP_R and Delta_k(T-v)=Delta_k(H)+Delta_{k-1}(R); consequently the original-leaf favorable selector and complete aggregate have the origin's exact A+B<0 and C-B representation, counting every leaf tag.
claims.scope: Universal exact identity for finite ordinary trees and every integer rank; no interior-rank sign or novelty conclusion.
claims.reason: The independent-set partition by the original support is a complete proof, including negative/terminal ranks and repeated-support leaf tags. The identity is an inherited elementary leaf-deletion recurrence and does not imply the target sign.

claims.statement: Independent symbolic integer calculations give, at p=alpha-2, P60: alpha=30, x=17, two favorable leaves each with selector -35495 and summand -165851, S=-331702; T60: alpha=182, x=87, one marked favorable leaf with selector -359 and summand -15930 and 180 arm favorable leaves each with selector -181 and summand -16287, S=-2947590.
claims.scope: Exactly the stated P60 and 243-vertex T60 constructions at their first-interior ranks; bounded computation only.
claims.reason: A new direct polynomial factorization, independent of the admitted evaluator, reproduces alpha, first strict descent, selectors, summands, and complete leaf-tag sums and asserts the branch polynomial equalities.

limitations: The branch identity and two negative complete-sum rows do not prove the universal first-interior inequality or refute it.
The historical pointwise and support-fibre failures in a wider rank window do not establish a failure at p=alpha-2.
